questions.text: Why does the Pix2Pix discriminator receive both the input image x and the candidate output y?

options.A: To reconstruct x from y using the discriminator as a decoder.
options.B: To compute an exact conditional likelihood for each image pair.
options.C: To replace the generator's need for paired training examples.
options.D: To judge whether y looks realistic and is consistent with x.

questions.explanation: Conditioning the discriminator on the pair lets it assess compatibility with the input as well as output realism. Seeing only y would not let it directly judge that relationship.

questions.text: You have separate collections of summer and winter scenes with no matched image pairs. Which training setup is designed to learn translation between these domains without pairs?

options.A: Pix2Pix with an L1 loss against randomly selected winter targets.
options.B: CycleGAN with two generators and round-trip consistency losses.
options.C: An unconditional GAN with neither domain labels nor input images.
options.D: Pix2Pix with only a larger weight on paired reconstruction loss.

questions.explanation: CycleGAN learns mappings in both directions using unpaired domain samples and cycle consistency: F(G(x)) approximates x and G(F(y)) approximates y. Standard Pix2Pix requires aligned pairs; random targets do not provide that correspondence.

questions.text: This check compares generated and real means for each condition. What does it print?
questions.explanation: Class 0 generates mean +2 instead of -2, and class 1 generates mean -2 instead of +2. Both absolute errors are 4, so both checks fail. The pooled mean is nevertheless correct, showing why conditional checks matter.
